purpose: Contextual review hypotheses, not automatic beauty scores. Trial rules require screenshot evidence and independent validation before promotion.

rules.appliesWhen: A command is a primary reading or copying object in a narrow layout.
rules.observation: A short command word is split into isolated characters while nearby controls keep fixed width.
rules.impact: The user must reconstruct the command instead of scanning it as a coherent object.
rules.hypothesis: Allocate command and action separate narrow-screen tracks before shrinking type.
changes: Move copy action below the command at narrow widths.
Preserve command tokens; use explicit local scrolling for unusually long commands.
Check component padding, action width and command typography tokens together.
rules.positiveCase: SuperCLI 390px light default, observed 2026-10-26: final g in wrangler wraps to its own line. This is a failure case motivating the rule, not a validated improved result.
rules.counterexample: An intentionally multiline shell pipeline with complete tokens may improve readability; a single line is not universally required.
verify: Same build, route, theme and width; inspect short and long commands.
Keyboard focus and copy feedback stay reachable.
No page overflow; declared command-local scrolling is acceptable.
rules.promotionEvidence: Needs comparable before/after screenshots, action checks and an independent reviewer; current evidence only supports a trial hypothesis.

rules.appliesWhen: The product declares a token system shared across components or themes.
rules.observation: The same semantic role drifts across components or states without a documented reason.
rules.impact: Hierarchy and status become inconsistent, and changes acquire hidden side effects.
rules.hypothesis: Trace primitive value → semantic alias → component/state usage before adding new values.
changes: Document purpose, type, source, theme and component consumer.
Use semantic roles for text, surfaces, actions and status.
Keep product-specific exceptions explicit and review their impact.
rules.positiveCase: A repeated primary action acquires an unrelated hover color through a local literal; source trace can demonstrate the drift.
rules.counterexample: Several semantic aliases can intentionally resolve to the same value. Equal computed colors do not prove redundant tokens, and many computed colors do not prove source literals.
verify: Inspect token definitions and actual component references, not just computed color counts.
Check normal, focus, selected and disabled states in declared themes.
rules.promotionEvidence: Requires source-traced examples and counterexamples from more than one product type.

rules.appliesWhen: The product contract names a first-read object and primary action.
rules.observation: Repeated decoration or equal-weight secondary objects compete with the user's first decision.
rules.impact: The user must search for the next useful action despite the page appearing polished.
rules.hypothesis: Redistribute size, position, contrast and spacing in favor of the task's first decision.
changes: Promote the first-read object rather than enlarging every component.
Group supporting metrics and separate primary from secondary actions.
Retain a distinctive domain object or interaction rather than adding generic decoration.
rules.positiveCase: A monitoring screen hides the failed job and recovery action beneath four equal KPI cards; this is a hypothetical case to validate.
rules.counterexample: An editorial cover may deliberately prioritize atmosphere and title before navigation; copying monitoring-screen density would damage that task.
verify: A new reviewer identifies the intended object and next action in the screenshot.
Preserve the same task at narrow widths and in long-content states.
rules.promotionEvidence: Needs real task-oriented studies and independently reviewed before/after cases; hypothetical examples alone are insufficient.

rules.appliesWhen: A project directory renders one representative visual per entry and the visitor must recognise which project it belongs to.
rules.observation: The entry's visual renders successfully and passes low-level checks, yet shows an abstract gradient, a mood render or a generic mascot that identifies no particular product.
rules.impact: The visitor sees a polished but meaningless image and cannot connect the card to the project it claims to represent.
rules.hypothesis: Classify the visual by what it depicts, then route only the unrecognisable ones to human review; never let a model verdict decide on its own.
changes: Classify the visual into brand mark, product-form render, interface screenshot, abstract mood image or text-only cover.
Treat the model's classification as a lead, not a verdict; a reviewer confirms or overturns it.
Judge emptiness by decoded-pixel statistics rather than byte-level entropy.
rules.positiveCase: Blog project directory, 24 entries audited 2026-10-29 on a local 4B VLM: 9 passed outright, 6 were flagged for human review, 3 failed low-level checks and 6 images failed to load. Confirmed true positives by eye include codex-manager (a shiba-inu sticker that identifies no product), museav and museav-mcp (abstract renders). Confirmed false positives include usage-statusline (a real colour-card render) and kyvault (a promo image whose caption names the tool), so the flag cannot be treated as a verdict.
rules.counterexample: A deliberate editorial or portfolio cover may legitimately prioritise atmosphere over legibility of the product; a reading-oriented site can ship an abstract visual without losing meaning. Product-form renders that omit any real interface can still be the correct choice for a tool that has no interface.
verify: Same entry set, same build and same thumbnails across runs.
A reviewer who has not seen the model's answer classifies each flagged image independently.
Re-run the classification at least three times and confirm the category does not drift.
rules.promotionEvidence: Evidence currently covers 24 entries on one product surface with a single reviewer and no independent second reviewer, so the rule stays at trial. Needs cross-product checks and an independent reviewer before promotion.
